mathgap.title: Signed Difference Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Interpret any phrase of the form 'the difference between the number of X and Y' as the signed subtraction X − Y, preserving the order as written.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement mentions 'difference between the number of ... and ...'.
mathgap.example: Treating 'difference between the number of A and B' as |A − B| (absolute value) instead of A − B.

mathgap.title: Directed More-Than Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Translate statements like 'A has N more than B' (including combined forms) into the equation A = B + N.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement uses 'more than' (or 'fewer than') to compare two persons.
mathgap.example: Assuming 'A has N more than B' forces A > B and discarding solutions where A − B is negative.

mathgap.title: Immediate Direct Assignment Update
mathgap.principle: When a direct count statement 'A has N items' appears, set A’s current count to N at that moment; later statements (including transfers) may modify it.
mathgap.example: Considering a direct count as a fixed initial value that cannot be changed by later transfers.

mathgap.title: Temporal Consistency of Transfers and Relational Statements
mathgap.principle: Process statements in order; apply each transfer immediately before evaluating any later relational statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a transfer statement is encountered.
mathgap.example: Delaying the effect of transfer statements until after all other statements have been processed.

mathgap.title: Full Difference Equality Interpretation
mathgap.principle: For statements equating one difference to another, translate them into (A − B) = (C − D), preserving the order on each side.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says 'the number of X that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of X that C and D have'.
mathgap.example: Misinterpreting a difference equality as a direct assignment to a single variable, ignoring the second term.

mathgap.title: Switch (Swap)
mathgap.principle: When a statement says two persons 'switch' their items, exchange their current counts without altering any other counts.
mathgap.example: Treating a swap as a transfer of a fixed amount rather than exchanging the whole counts.

mathgap.title: Quantity Modification (Multiplication and Subtraction)
mathgap.principle: When a statement says a person 'eats N' of an item, subtract N from their count; when it says a person 'receives N' or 'gets N', add N.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering verbs that indicate a quantity change (e.g., eats, receives, gets).
mathgap.example: Failing to subtract when a person eats items, leaving the count unchanged.

mathgap.title: Temporal Snapshot for Relational Statements
mathgap.principle: Treat each relational statement as a constraint on the counts at the moment it appears; do not later retroactively adjust those constraints.
mathgap.example: Applying later transfers retroactively to earlier relational equations.

mathgap.title: Conditional Transfer of All Items
mathgap.principle: For any transfer statement, apply it immediately. If the statement is unconditional ('X gives N to Y'), move N items from X to Y. If it is conditional of the form 'If X has more than Y items, X will transfer their items to Z', evaluate the condition using the current counts at that point; if true, move all of X’s items to Z (setting X’s count to zero).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering any transfer statement, whether unconditional or conditional.
mathgap.example: Applying a conditional transfer regardless of the condition, or moving only a fixed amount when the statement says 'transfer their items' (i.e., moving only N instead of all).

mathgap.description: Treating ‘difference between the number of X and Y’ as absolute value instead of signed subtraction.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrase 'difference between' is ambiguous, and the model often defaults to an absolute‑value interpretation.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always keep the order of the two quantities as written and compute X − Y, not |X − Y|.

mathgap.description: Delaying the effect of transfer statements until after all other statements have been processed.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model tends to batch updates and forgets that transfers happen at a specific point in the narrative.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer immediately when it is read, before processing any later relational statements.

mathgap.description: Assuming ‘A has N more than B’ forces A > B and discarding solutions where A − B is negative.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The wording 'more than' is interpreted as a strict inequality, leading the model to reject valid negative differences.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat 'A has N more than B' as the equation A = B + N, allowing the difference to be negative if later constraints imply it.

mathgap.description: Considering a direct count as a fixed initial value that cannot be changed by later transfers.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats direct counts as immutable initial conditions rather than current values at that point.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Update the count at the moment of the direct statement, but allow later transfers to modify it.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting a difference equality as a direct assignment to a single variable, ignoring the second term.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model simplifies the equality (A − B) = (C − D) to A = C, dropping the subtraction parts.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Translate the whole equality as (A − B) = (C − D) and keep both terms on each side.

mathgap.description: Applying later transfers retroactively to earlier relational equations.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model updates earlier constraints after processing later transfers, violating the snapshot nature of relational statements.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat each relational statement as a snapshot; once an equation is recorded, do not modify it based on later events.
